requirements.original: The communication operations (see clause 22) `send, receive, trigger, call, getcall, reply, getreply` and raise and connection operations connect, map, disconnect and unmap (see clause 21.1) are exceptions to the weaker rule of type compatibility and require strong typing.
requirements.canonical: The communication operations `send`, `receive`, `trigger`, `call`, `getcall`, `reply`, `getreply` and `raise` SHALL apply strong typing instead of type compatibility.

ambiguity.issue: The list omits `catch` (and `check`), while 6.3.4-s003/s004 treat `catch` like `raise`. Chose the literal list.
readings: Only the listed operations `send`, `receive`, `trigger`, `call`, `getcall`, `reply`, `getreply` and `raise` SHALL apply strong typing.
All communication operations of clause 22, including `catch` and `check`, SHALL apply strong typing.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.4 -- The communication operations (see clause 22) `send, receive, trigger, call, getcall, reply, getreply` and raise and connection operations connect, map, disconnect and unmap (see clause 21.1) are exceptions to the weaker rule of type compatibility and require strong typing.

requirements.original: The communication operations (see clause 22) `send, receive, trigger, call, getcall, reply, getreply` and raise and connection operations connect, map, disconnect and unmap (see clause 21.1) are exceptions to the weaker rule of type compatibility and require strong typing.
requirements.canonical: The connection operations `connect`, `map`, `disconnect` and `unmap` SHALL apply strong typing instead of type compatibility.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.4 -- The communication operations (see clause 22) `send, receive, trigger, call, getcall, reply, getreply` and raise and connection operations connect, map, disconnect and unmap (see clause 21.1) are exceptions to the weaker rule of type compatibility and require strong typing.

requirements.original: The types of values or templates directly used as parameters of the operations send, receive and trigger shall also be explicitly defined in the associated port type definition.
requirements.canonical: The type of a value or template used directly as argument of a `send`, `receive` or `trigger` operation SHALL be explicitly listed in the definition of the port type of the port the operation is applied to.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.4 -- The types of values or templates directly used as parameters of the operations send, receive and trigger shall also be explicitly defined in the associated port type definition.

requirements.original: The signature type of the parameter list given to the operations call, getcall, reply, getreply and the signature type given to the operations catch and raise shall also be explicitly defined in the associated port type definition.
requirements.canonical: The signature of the parameter list given to a `call`, `getcall`, `reply` or `getreply` operation, and the signature given to a `catch` or `raise` operation, SHALL be explicitly listed in the definition of the port type of the port the operation is applied to.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.4 -- The signature type of the parameter list given to the operations call, getcall, reply, getreply and the signature type given to the operations catch and raise shall also be explicitly defined in the associated port type definition.

requirements.original: The types of values or templates directly used as exceptions to the operations catch and raise shall be explicitly defined in the exceptions part of the definition of the signature given to the operation.
requirements.canonical: The type of a value or template used directly as exception in a `catch` or `raise` operation SHALL be explicitly listed in the exception list of the signature given to the operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.4 -- The types of values or templates directly used as exceptions to the operations catch and raise shall be explicitly defined in the exceptions part of the definition of the signature given to the operation.

requirements.original: p.receive (MyRec:?); // shall not match as the transmitted template is of the alias type and not of the user-defined type
requirements.canonical: A `receive` operation whose template is of a type "T" SHALL NOT match a message that was sent as a value or template of a different type, even if that type is a synonym of type "T".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.4 -- p.receive (MyRec:?); // shall not match as the transmitted template is of the alias type and not of the user-defined type

requirements.original: var MyRec v_x; p.receive (MyRecAlias:?) -> value v_x; // shall not cause an error since storing the value requires no strong typing
requirements.canonical: Storing the value of a received message in a variable by a value redirect IS NOT subject to strong typing; the variable needs only be of a compatible type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.4 -- var MyRec v_x; p.receive (MyRecAlias:?) -> value v_x; // shall not cause an error since storing the value requires no strong typing

requirements.original: If it is necessary to convert values of one type to values of another type, because their types have different root types, then either one of the predefined conversion functions defined in clause 16.1.2 or a user defined function shall be used.
requirements.canonical: When a value has to be converted to a type with a different root type, the conversion SHALL use one of the predefined conversion functions of clause 16.1.2 or a user-defined function.
requirements.condition: the source and target types have different root types

examples.text:

  MyHstring := int2hex(123, 4);

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.5 -- If it is necessary to convert values of one type to values of another type, because their types have different root types, then either one of the predefined conversion functions defined in clause 16.1.2 or a user defined function shall be used.

requirements.original: For variables, constants and parameters of port types, the reference to a port "b" of type "B" is compatible to type "A" if type "B" and type "A" are equal or synonym types.
requirements.canonical: A reference to a port "b" of port type "B" IS compatible with port type "A" (for variables, constants and parameters of port types) only if type "B" and type "A" are equal or synonym types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.6 -- For variables, constants and parameters of port types, the reference to a port "b" of type "B" is compatible to type "A" if type "B" and type "A" are equal or synonym types.

requirements.original: For variables, constants and parameters of timer types, the reference to a timer is compatible with any other timer reference.
requirements.canonical: A timer reference IS compatible with any other timer reference (for variables, constants and parameters of timer types).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.7 -- For variables, constants and parameters of timer types, the reference to a timer is compatible with any other timer reference.

requirements.original: map types are only compatible with other map types.
requirements.canonical: A map type IS NOT compatible with any type other than a map type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.8 -- map types are only compatible with other map types.

requirements.original: A value "b" of a map type "B" is compatible with a map type "A" if the from type of "A" is compatible with the from type of "B" and the to type of "B" is compatible with the to type of "A".
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of map type "B" IS compatible with map type "A" if the from type of "A" is compatible with the from type of "B" and the to type of "B" is compatible with the to type of "A".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.8 -- A value "b" of a map type "B" is compatible with a map type "A" if the from type of "A" is compatible with the from type of "B" and the to type of "B" is compatible with the to type of "A".

requirements.original: // every value of Map2 can be used in a variable of Map1 but access to values associated with keys that are not charstring values is not possible
requirements.canonical: When a value of map type "B" is used in a variable of map type "A" whose from type is narrower, values associated with keys that are not values of the from type of "A" CANNOT be accessed through the variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.8 -- // every value of Map2 can be used in a variable of Map1 but access to values associated with keys that are not charstring values is not possible

requirements.original: A type can be defined as a synonym to another type.
requirements.canonical: A type MAY be defined as a synonym of another type.

examples.text: type MyType1 MyType2; // MyType2 is synonym to MyType1

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.4 -- A type can be defined as a synonym to another type.

requirements.original: Type synonyms can be defined for all kinds of types.
requirements.canonical: A type synonym MAY be defined for every kind of type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.4 -- Type synonyms can be defined for all kinds of types.

requirements.original: Synonym types are compatible.
requirements.canonical: Synonym types ARE compatible with each other.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.4 -- Synonym types are compatible.

requirements.original: Automatic types are used in variable, constant and module parameter declarations.
requirements.canonical: The automatic type MAY be used only in a variable declaration, a template variable declaration, a constant declaration or a module parameter declaration.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence is descriptive; it is unclear whether the list is exhaustive (other declarations, e.g. formal parameters or templates, are excluded) and whether template variable declarations count as variable declarations (the examples use `var template`). Chose the exhaustive reading including template variables.
readings: The automatic type MAY be used only in variable (including template variable), constant and module parameter declarations.
The automatic type MAY be used at least in variable, constant and module parameter declarations; other uses are not addressed.

examples.text:
function f_isEven(integer p_par) return boolean { return p_par mod 2 == 0; }
 type enumerated Colour { yellow, red, blue, green }
 var integer v_int := 1;
 var v_automaticA := v_int; // automatic integer type
 var v_automaticB := f_isEven(5); // automatic boolean type
 var v_automaticC := match(5, ?); // automatic boolean type
 var v_automaticD := v_int + 6; // automatic integer type
 var v_automaticE := '0010'B; // automatic bitstring type
 var v_automaticF := "abc"; // automatic charstring type
 var template v_automaticG := integer:?; // automatic integer type
 var v_automaticH := Colour.red; // automatic enumerated type
 var v_automaticI := {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}; // automatic record of integer type

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- Automatic types are used in variable, constant and module parameter declarations.

requirements.original: When used, the type part of these declarations is skipped and the type is provided implicitly.
requirements.canonical: A variable, constant or module parameter declaration that uses the automatic type IS written without the type part.
requirements.condition: the declaration uses the automatic type

requirements.condition: all indexes are of the integer type and all item values have a common type

ambiguity.issue: "index assignment notation" is used for the glossary term "index notation".

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- k) Index assignment notation where all indexes are of the integer type and all item values have a common type shall provide an automatic type record of _{common type}.

requirements.original: The common type shall fulfil requirements_ for automatic typing.
requirements.canonical: The common type of the item values of an index notation with integer indexes used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- The common type shall fulfil requirements_ for automatic typing.

requirements.original: l) Index assignment notation where all indexes have a common type in case the type is different from the integer type and all item values have a common type shall provide an automatic type map from _{common type of the indexes} to_ _{common type of the values}.
requirements.canonical: An index notation used for automatic typing in which all indexes have a common type other than `integer` and all item values have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `map from` the common index type `to` the common value type.
requirements.condition: all indexes have a common non-integer type and all item values have a common type

ambiguity.issue: "index assignment notation" is used for the glossary term "index notation".

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- l) Index assignment notation where all indexes have a common type in case the type is different from the integer type and all item values have a common type shall provide an automatic type map from _{common type of the indexes} to_ _{common type of the values}.

requirements.original: The common type of the indexes and the_ common type of the values shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing.
requirements.canonical: The common type of the indexes and the common type of the item values of an index notation with non-integer indexes used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- The common type of the indexes and the_ common type of the values shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing.

requirements.original: m) List of templates with two or more items and complemented list of templates where all templates have a common type shall provide automatic type that is equal to the common type.
requirements.canonical: A template list with two or more items or a complemented template list, in which all templates have a common type, SHALL provide an automatic type equal to the common type.
requirements.condition: all templates in the list have a common type

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether "with two or more items" also applies to the complemented list, and "and" means "or" here. Chose the reading that the minimum of two items applies only to the template list.
readings: A template list with two or more items, or a complemented template list with any number of items, SHALL provide the common type as automatic type.
A template list or a complemented template list SHALL provide the common type as automatic type only if it has two or more items.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- m) List of templates with two or more items and complemented list of templates where all templates have a common type shall provide automatic type that is equal to the common type.

requirements.original: The common type shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing.
requirements.canonical: The common type of the templates of a template list or complemented template list used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- The common type shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing.

requirements.original: n) Value range.
requirements.canonical: The template body used for automatic typing MAY be a value range.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- n) Value range.

requirements.original: The automatic type is equal to the type of the bounds.
requirements.canonical: The automatic type of a value range IS equal to the type of its bounds.

ambiguity.issue: The rule does not say what happens when one bound is infinity or when the bounds have different types. Chose the reading that the type of the non-infinite bound(s) is used.
readings: The automatic type of a value range IS the type of its finite bound(s); bounds of different types are an error.
The automatic type of a value range IS the common type of both bounds, determined by the expression rules.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- The automatic type is equal to the type of the bounds.

requirements.original: If both bounds are set to infinity, the integer type is provided.
requirements.canonical: If both bounds of a value range used for automatic typing are infinity, the automatic type IS `integer`.
requirements.condition: both bounds are set to infinity
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- If both bounds are set to infinity, the integer type is provided.

requirements.original: o) Pattern.
requirements.canonical: The template body used for automatic typing MAY be a pattern.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- o) Pattern.

requirements.original: If the pattern contains only characters or references of the charstring type, the automatic type is charstring, otherwise it is universal charstring.
requirements.canonical: If a pattern used for automatic typing contains only characters or references of the `charstring` type, the automatic type IS `charstring`.
requirements.condition: the pattern contains only characters or references of the charstring type
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- If the pattern contains only characters or references of the charstring type, the automatic type is charstring, otherwise it is universal charstring.

requirements.original: If the pattern contains only characters or references of the charstring type, the automatic type is charstring, otherwise it is universal charstring.
requirements.canonical: If a pattern used for automatic typing contains a character or reference that is not of the `charstring` type, the automatic type IS `universal charstring`.
requirements.condition: the pattern contains a character or reference not of the charstring type
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- If the pattern contains only characters or references of the charstring type, the automatic type is charstring, otherwise it is universal charstring.

requirements.original: p) Superset and subset where all items have a common type shall provide an automatic type set of _{common_ _type}.
requirements.canonical: A `superset` or `subset` matching mechanism in which all items have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `set of` the common type.
requirements.condition: all items have a common type

ambiguity.issue: "Superset and subset" means either of the two matching mechanisms.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- p) Superset and subset where all items have a common type shall provide an automatic type set of _{common_ _type}.

requirements.original: The common type shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing._ q) Any other TTCN-3 language operation that can occur on the right-hand side of an assignment where the type context is unambiguous.
requirements.canonical: The common type of the items of a `superset` or `subset` matching mechanism used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- The common type shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing._ q) Any other TTCN-3 language operation that can occur on the right-hand side of an assignment where the type context is unambiguous.

requirements.original: The common type shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing._ q) Any other TTCN-3 language operation that can occur on the right-hand side of an assignment where the type context is unambiguous.
requirements.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be any other TTCN-3 language operation that can occur on the right-hand side of an assignment, if its type context is unambiguous.

ambiguity.issue: With an automatic type there is no declared type that provides a type context, so it is unclear which operations qualify; the item is open-ended. Chose the reading that the operation itself must determine its type unambiguously.
readings: Any operation whose result type is determined by the operation itself MAY be used for automatic typing.
Any operation MAY be used for automatic typing if an enclosing construct provides an unambiguous type context.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- The common type shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing._ q) Any other TTCN-3 language operation that can occur on the right-hand side of an assignment where the type context is unambiguous.

requirements.original: var template v_automaticErr := ?; // Causes an error as the ? symbol doesn't provide a type
requirements.canonical: The template body of a declaration that uses the automatic type SHALL NOT consist only of the AnyValue matching symbol `?`, because `?` does not provide a type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.5 -- var template v_automaticErr := ?; // Causes an error as the ? symbol doesn't provide a type
